title: GWM Ora 5 Lux EV from $32,990 Driveaway @ GWM
body:
Deal: GWM Ora 5 Lux EV from $32,990 Driveaway @ GWM

[cycleri3] This manufacturer sneakily claims WLTC range not WLTP. WLTC is a test cycle within the WLTP range test.
I wouldn't expect this 435km WLTC range comparable to other cars reporting WLTP. I expect it to be around 375 WLTP roughly but that's just a guess.
[4agte] Check CarSauce on YouTube to see what they claim
[Jugganautx] carsauce is full of shit, and feeds off gullible people like you to take his reviews seriously.
[NervousValuable] You’re not wrong. I recently drove my partners Ora 5 from Sydney to Mudgee (285km). Battery was drained to 15%. It definitely felt like 50-100km range was not accounted for as we were under the impression the range was 435km.
[cycleri3] not too bad, I am assuming this is a 110km/h highway drive mostly? Cars don't get their WLTP range at highway speeds usually, about 15% less. Even more if you are climbing elevation or there are heavy cross winds or tail wind. My family members Xpeng G6 has 570km range, it gets roughly that in the city, its around 420-440km on highway and it only gave about 380km in the outback on the Stewart highway.
[rooster7777] @Consumer123: Sounds even more like you should pay more attention to what you need, and the specs of a car… instead of spitting out bollocks
Should a person using an ev for urban commuting keep buying petrol until an ev has a 600km range?
Like any consumer choice… buy what's fit for purpose
[Consumer123] @rooster7777: If you don't travel long very often you'd be much better not owing a car at all.
If they are able to sell low range cars at such prices they won't have much of motivation to go higher on the range at an affordable price..
Certainly everyone has a different need but a car should serve all your travel needs, be it short or long.. moreover a 200km travel isn't very long in Australia and much of suburban Melbourne is all up and down..
Surprising to see how fanatic people have become about electric cars..
[rooster7777] @Consumer123: If you don't travel far and there is public transport or safe bike lanes you'd be better off not owning a car at all….agreed. Absolutely nothing to do with the range of an ev, or if you would use an ICE
A car should suit all your travel purposes…. yeah…all cars should be capable of towing a caravan, a car on a trailer, a large boat, and fitting into a small parking lot in an underground garage…. stupid logic there.
200km is a long way if you commute 10 or 20 or 30km a day etc etc a stupid thing to say
Melbourne is up and down…. not as much as your logic.
YOU are surprised at "how fanatic people have become about evs". Not the rest of the world, just you. Are you surprised you don't have to employ someone with a red flag to walk in front of your car?
Are you surprised that people use the internet, and mobile phones?
[greater mimic] @Consumer123: If you're driving 200km on the regular then sure get something else, but comparing that to slightly hilly suburban driving is silly
[npnp] That's actually not bad. I drive a model 3 and despite being a more efficient car it would also give somewhere around that figure in real world. That's the reality of EVs. They are efficient around town, not so much in highways.
[bargaino] In this context they are the same thing. WLTC is not one of the tests, it is the test cycle.
During a WLTP test, the vehicle is run on a dynamometer following the WLTC driving cycle, which lasts 30 minutes and covers a distance of 23.35 km at an average speed of 46.5 km/h (with peak speeds exceeding 131 km/h).
WLTP/C tends to be accurate for city driving, but you'll get 15-20% less range at highway speed.
[cycleri3] If they are the same, why aren't they reporting WLTP? Clearly they want to show the higher range number so they are claiming WLTC.
[mcgrathkerr] Heres the data
The ORA 5 SUV is powered by a 58.33kWh battery delivering up to 435km of WLTC range and a consumption figure of just 15.5kWh/100km
58/15.5 x 100 = 375 km max. I imagine highway driving is worst.
[RedSky1] Good rule of thumb is WLTP x 0.8 at 105-110km/h highway in decent weather conditions.
so about 350km max highway from full (100%) to empty (0%)
rain, headwinds, mountainous driving or really cold conditions = less still
[Legendalvin] I was told after an OTA update recently, the fully charged range shows 350-380km instead of 435 , can any owner confirm ?
[RomanBogan] I have ordered an Ultra version. Suggest those who are still in denial just go and test drive one. It is a Porsche from Temu but does the same thing transporting you from point A to point B 10 times cheaper with 7 year warranty and 8 year warranty on its battery. You can’t buy an EV and expect it to perform like petrol one and deliver cost savings over the petrol one, it will never pay for itself. Buy a new car when you really need one and it can help to save your tax..
[MrZ] $27,990 on FB Marketplace, with 2,000 km on the clock: https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/1088341947410548/?…
[bargaino] plus stamp duty, sounds right. "Lose 15% when you drive it off the lot".
[MrZ] About $29,200 with stamp duty, yes. And probably less than 12 months rego too.
Note that Ora/Ora 5 resale is quite a bit worse than the industry average. Think before you buy when it comes to these Chinese cars. Resale is more important to consider than initial purchase price.
[plmko] Having sold a Chinese EV my advice is to forget resell value and focus on sell-ability. It doesn't help you that the market says it is worth XYZ but your listing sits there for more than a month and you go through a fair few buyers. In end I had to drop it by an extra $1k despite already being the cheapest.
[andresampras] @plmko: So many variables aside from ‘Chinese’.
What car was it?
[xyron] These are ex-demos being sold by Astoria GWM in Brighton. They aren't used cars. Although I do find it odd when dealers try to advertise on Facebook Marketplace
[djmm] Hows the ANCAP on all these Chinese electric car brands in general?
[Save 50 Cent] 5 usually means annoying beeping even if you yawn or sneeze.
[ONEMariachi] This one wasn’t actually that bad compared to others when I test drove it, you could turn most of them off. It did have a weird whining noose while driving though that I didn’t notice on the Gac or byd’s i’ve tested.
The white leather everywhere on the model i tested also was god awful. Felt like I was driving in a bubble and was really distracting.
[E5TOQUE] Out of the Chinese brands GWM, BYD, MG and Xpeng have their safety systems dialled in well now.
GWM has invested heavily in Australian ride/handling/tuning (ex Holden engineers working with them now)
BYD has rolled out a number of updates that have addressed things. They have the sales numbers to back the improvements.
MG has gone a step further with quick shortcut menu options to disable everything.
And the likes of Xpeng have got safety systems up at the level of Tesla. They review well.
All the others…. yeah they have issues. Less investment.
